test_text.title: Green Wave Washes Over Mainstream Shopping

article.title: Green Wave Washes Over Mainstream Shopping

items.sentence_raw: Research in Britain has shown that green consumers continue to flourish as a significant group amongst shoppers.
items.explain: Q1: The passage says *'green consumers continue to flourish as a significant group amongst shoppers'* — this is about **commercial** trends, not **political** ones. So the answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: This suggests that politicians who claim environmentalism is yesterday's issue may be seriously misjudging the public mood.
items.explain: Q7: The passage says politicians *'may be seriously misjudging the public mood'* because a *'green wave'* has taken in *'people previously untouched by environmental concerns'* — this means **more widespread interest** than they thought. Option **B** matches this. ***Option A is a trap*** — the passage says the green wave happened *'despite recession'*, not because politicians are pre-occupied with it. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: A report from Mintel, the market research organisation, says that despite recession and financial pressures, more people than ever want to buy environmentally friendly products and a 'green wave' has swept through consumerism, taking in people previously untouched by environmental concerns.
items.explain:
Q2: The passage says *'despite recession and financial pressures, more people than ever want to buy environmentally friendly products'* — **'despite'** means even with money problems, people still buy green. The question says being **'financially better off'** made them more sensitive, but the passage shows the opposite. So the answer is **NO**.

Q7: The passage says politicians *'may be seriously misjudging the public mood'* because a *'green wave'* has taken in *'people previously untouched by environmental concerns'* — this means **more widespread interest** than they thought. Option **B** matches this. ***Option A is a trap*** — the passage says the green wave happened *'despite recession'*, not because politicians are pre-occupied with it. So the answer is **B**.

Q8: The passage directly calls Mintel *'the market research organisation'* — **'market research'** means a **business survey organisation**. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: The recently published report also predicts that the process will repeat itself with 'ethical' concerns, involving issues such as fair trade with the Third World and the social record of businesses.
items.explain: Q13: The passage says the report predicts concerns will involve *'the social record of businesses'* — **'social record'** is what companies must think more carefully about. So the answer is **K**.

items.sentence_raw: Companies will have to be more honest and open in response to this mood.
items.explain: Q10: The passage says *'Companies will have to be more honest and open in response to this mood'* — **'honest and open'** means **'honesty and openness'**. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: Mintel's survey, based on nearly 1,000 consumers, found that the proportion who look for green products and are prepared to pay more for them has climbed from 53 per cent in 1990 to around 60 per cent in 1994.
items.explain:
Q3: The passage says *'the proportion who look for green products and are prepared to pay more for them has climbed from 53 per cent in 1990 to around 60 per cent in 1994'* — **60 per cent** is the **'majority'**. So the answer is **YES**.

Q5: The passage says Mintel's survey was *'based on nearly 1,000 consumers'* — this is a general group, not limited to **'professional and managerial groups'**. The question says they **'limited'** their investigation, but the passage shows they included many types. So the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: On average, they will pay 13 per cent more for such products, although this percentage is higher among women, managerial and professional groups and those aged 35 to 44.

Between 1990 and 1994 the proportion of consumers claiming to be unaware of or unconcerned about green issues fell from 18 to 10 per cent but the number of green spenders among older people and manual workers has risen substantially.
Regions such as Scotland have also caught up with the south of England in their environmental concerns.
According to Mintel, the image of green consumerism as associated in the past with the more eccentric members of society has virtually disappeared.
The consumer research manager for Mintel, Angela Hughes, said it had become firmly established as a mainstream market.
She explained that as far as the average person is concerned environmentalism has not "gone off the boil".
In fact, it has spread across a much wider range of consumer groups, ages and occupations.

Mintel's 1994 survey found that 13 per cent of consumers are 'very dark green', nearly always buying environmentally friendly products, 28 per cent are 'dark green', trying 'as far as possible' to buy such products, and 21 per cent are 'pale green' - tending to buy green products if they see them.
Another 26 per cent are 'armchair greens'; they said they care about environmental issues but their concern does not affect their spending habits.
items.explain: Q9: The passage says *'armchair greens'* are people who *'care about environmental issues but their concern does not affect their spending habits'* — this means they express concern without **actively supporting** principles. Option **C** matches exactly. ***Option A is a trap*** — **'ethical spenders'** actually buy goods, they don't just sit and care. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: Only 10 per cent say they do not care about green issues.
Four in ten people are 'ethical spenders', buying goods which do not, for example, involve dealings with oppressive regimes.
This figure is the same as in 1990, although the number of 'armchair ethicals' has risen from 28 to 35 per cent and only 22 per cent say they are unconcerned now, against 30 per cent in 1990.
items.explain: Q12: The passage says *'the number of armchair ethicals has risen from 28 to 35 per cent'* — this is a growth in **'armchair ethicals'**. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: Hughes claims that in the twenty-first century, consumers will be encouraged to think more about the entire history of the products and services they buy, including the policies of the companies that provide them and that this will require a greater degree of honesty with consumers.
items.explain: Q11: The passage says *'consumers will be encouraged to think more about the entire history of the products'* — this shows the increased awareness is among **'consumers'**. So the answer is **F**.

items.sentence_raw: Among green consumers, animal testing is the top issue - 48 per cent said they would be deterred from buying a product it if had been tested on animals - followed by concerns regarding irresponsible selling, the ozone layer, river and sea pollution, forest destruction, recycling and factory farming.
However, concern for specific issues is lower than in 1990, suggesting that many consumers feel that Government and business have taken on the environmental agenda.

orphan_explain_map.4: Q4: The passage talks about Mintel's **findings** on green shopping habits, but it never says these findings **influence** consumers. ***NOT GIVEN is not the same as FALSE*** — the passage simply does not mention this connection. So the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
orphan_explain_map.6: Q6: The passage mentions surveys from **1990** and **1994**, but it never says Mintel does surveys **every year**. ***Do not assume a pattern from just two dates***. So the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
